los.text: Demonstrate a structured respiratory examination and identify abnormal findings
los.html:
1Introduction, consent, sit at 45°, expose the chest.
2. General inspectionBreathlessness, accessory muscles, cyanosis, cachexia, around the bed (inhalers, oxygen, sputum pot).
3. HandsClubbing, tar staining, peripheral cyanosis, CO₂ retention flap, wasting of small muscles (Pancoast); pulse, respiratory rate.
4. Face and neckCentral cyanosis (tongue), Horner's, JVP, lymph nodes, trachea (deviation).
5. Chest inspectionShape (barrel, pectus), scars, symmetry.
6. PalpationChest expansion (front and back), apex beat, tactile fremitus.
7. PercussionCompare both sides, top to bottom, including the axillae.
8. AuscultationBreath sounds, added sounds, vocal resonance.
9. BackRepeat inspection, expansion, percussion, auscultation; check for sacral and ankle oedema.
10. FinishPeak flow, sats, sputum, observations, CXR.
FindingConsolidationEffusionPneumothoraxCollapse
TracheaCentralAway (if large)Away (tension)Towards
ExpansionReducedReducedReducedReduced
PercussionDullStony dullHyper-resonantDull
Breath soundsBronchial, cracklesReduced/absentReduced/absentReduced
Vocal resonanceIncreasedReducedReducedReduced

los.text: Conduct a focused history for a patient presenting with respiratory symptoms
los.html:
AreaQuestions
CoughDuration (acute <3 weeks, chronic >8 weeks), dry or productive, timing (night: asthma, heart failure)
SputumColour, amount, blood (haemoptysis)
BreathlessnessOnset, exercise tolerance, orthopnoea, PND, MRC dyspnoea grade
Chest painPleuritic (sharp, worse breathing in)
Wheeze, fever, weight loss, night sweatsInfection, TB, cancer
Risk factorsSmoking (pack-years), occupation (asbestos), pets, travel, TB contacts, drugs (ACE inhibitors)
Red flagsHaemoptysis, weight loss, hoarseness, persistent cough in a smoker → urgent CXR (NICE)

los.text: Describe and demonstrate the key components of active listening during a patient consultation.
los.html:
ComponentHow
AttendingEye contact, open posture, leaning in slightly, put the pen down
SilenceAllow pauses: the patient often adds important information
EncouragingNods, "go on", "mm"
Paraphrasing / reflecting"It sounds like the cough is keeping you awake"
Picking up cuesVerbal and non-verbal hints of worry
SummarisingCheck understanding
Not interruptingLet the patient finish their story

los.text: Demonstrate the ability to identify clinical indications for oxygen therapy.
los.html:
• Give oxygen for hypoxaemia (below the target saturation), not for breathlessness alone.
IndicationTarget
Critical illness: cardiac arrest, shock, sepsis, anaphylaxis, major trauma, carbon monoxide poisoning15 L/min non-rebreather initially
Hypoxaemic acute illness (pneumonia, PE, asthma, heart failure)94–98%
Risk of hypercapnia (COPD, obesity, neuromuscular disease)88–92%
  • Not indicated if saturations are normal (e.g. uncomplicated MI, anxiety).

los.text: Differentiate between oxygen delivery devices and their clinical applications.
los.html:
DeviceOxygen deliveredUse
Nasal cannulae1–4 L/min (~24–40%)Mild hypoxaemia, comfortable, can eat and talk
Simple face mask5–10 L/min (~40–60%)Moderate; ≥5 L/min to avoid rebreathing CO₂
Venturi maskFixed 24%, 28%, 31%, 35%, 40%, 60%COPD: precise oxygen at risk of CO₂ retention
Non-rebreather mask with reservoir15 L/min (~60–90%)Critically ill
High-flow nasal oxygenUp to 60 L/min, humidifiedSevere hypoxaemia on wards/ICU
NebuliserDriven by oxygen (6–8 L/min) or airBronchodilators; use air in COPD with hypercapnia

los.text: Safely administer supplementary oxygen in accordance with safety protocols.
los.html:
• Safety: oxygen must be prescribed with a target range
    • check saturations regularly
    • no smoking or naked flames (fire risk)
    • secure cylinders
    • humidify high flows.
1Check the prescription, patient identity and target range.
2Explain to the patient and gain consent.
3Choose the device; attach to the correct flowmeter (oxygen, not air); set the flow.
4Fit the device, check comfort and that the reservoir bag inflates (non-rebreather).
5Monitor saturations, respiratory rate and the patient; adjust to target; document.
  • COPD: watch for drowsiness, headache, flap (CO₂ retention): check an ABG.
